holding_summary: Denies a preliminary injunction sought by an adjoining landowner to enforce a deed restriction limiting defendant's lot to 'one dwelling house,' for lack of privity of contract/estate and lack of proof the restriction was intended for plaintiff's benefit.
notes: Deed building-restriction dispute between adjoining landowners over erection of a factory addition vs. a dwelling house; no lodging, boarding, or compensated occupancy issue.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: Landlord's boarding-up of a doorway used by a liquor-store tenant constituted an actual eviction from part of the premises, suspending rent; acceptance of back rent after a dispossess warrant did not waive the tenant's eviction defense as to later rent, nor create a month-to-month tenancy.
notes: Ordinary commercial (liquor store) landlord-tenant eviction/rent dispute; no lodging or boarding house issue.

holding_summary: A 1873 deed covenant forbidding a 'tenement house' is construed in its ordinary popular sense, not per the 1867 statutory definition; modern luxury apartment buildings with private baths, electricity, and elevators do not violate the covenant even though occupied by more than three independent families.
notes: Deed-covenant construction of 'tenement house' vs. luxury apartment building; concerns multi-family occupancy classification, not compensated room/lodger letting or boarding-house regulation.

holding_summary: A widow with a devisee's interest in partnership real estate who acquiesced in a lease made by the surviving partner is estopped from later disputing its validity; the lessee in possession could not defeat ejectment by acquiring outstanding title from her.
notes: Partnership real property lease/ejectment/estoppel dispute; no lodging or boarding-house issue.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Evidence that a husband occupied and used property titled to his wife, paying taxes, assessments, and mortgage interest as rent, was sufficient to support finding a landlord-tenant relationship supporting an action for use and occupation; the statute of frauds is no defense once the tenant has entered and occupied under a parol lease longer than a year.
notes: Use-and-occupation dispute between spouses over premises used as a livery stable; not a dwelling-letting or lodging/boarding case.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A contract granting exclusive rights to produce a play permitted the producer to stage it only with its own company, not to sublicense stock theaters to produce it; injunction granted against such sublicensing.
notes: Theatrical production/licensing contract dispute; wholly unrelated to real property lodging or boarding-house doctrine.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A complaint pleading 'use and occupation' at a stated monthly rent, payable in advance, sufficiently alleged an express monthly tenancy; dismissal for supposedly needing to plead an express contract was error.
notes: Ordinary monthly house rental/pleading dispute over unpaid rent; tenant occupied continuously for two years, not a short-term lodging arrangement.

holding_summary: A tenant who erected a structure under an oral understanding it would remain his property lost his right to remove it by later accepting new leases that made no reservation of a removal right.
notes: Commercial premises fixture-removal dispute (business partnership occupying storefront); no lodging or boarding issue.

holding_summary: Overrules a demurrer to a libel complaint concerning a newspaper article about a police raid on plaintiff's boarding house for gambling, holding the article could reasonably be read to imply the plaintiff-keeper's own knowledge of the gambling, distinguishing cases where only the premises (not the individual) were libeled.
notes: Plaintiff is described as keeping a private boarding house, but the holding turns entirely on libel-pleading/inference doctrine, not on the legal character or regulation of boarding-house keeping; boarding house is incidental factual backdrop only.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A deed covenant barring uses that 'injuriously affect' adjoining residence property, coupled with an enumerated list of prohibited business uses, does not bar erection of a building with storerooms merely because store use might incidentally affect neighboring residential value.
notes: Deed building-restriction covenant dispute over commercial storefront use; not about lodging/boarding or paying occupants.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: A quarry company exercising due care in blasting to prepare its own land for lawful business use will not be enjoined merely because the incidental jarring disturbs neighboring residences.
notes: Nuisance/blasting injunction case; unrelated to lodging or boarding-house doctrine.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: A holographic will was admitted to probate as validly executed under French law because the decedent, though an American citizen, had abandoned his American domicile and established a French domicile before his death; French forced-heirship law limits the legatee to one-fourth of the estate given three surviving legitimate children.
notes: Probate/domicile dispute; mentions decedent living in 'hotels and furnished lodgings' only in passing while narrating his travels, not as a doctrinal point about lodging arrangements.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: A subtenant of commercial premises who accepted a new lease from a third party after foreclosure is thereafter estopped from denying that party's title as landlord in a subsequent dispossess proceeding.
notes: Commercial subtenancy/estoppel-to-deny-title dispute over storefront premises; no lodging or boarding issue.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Constructive (not actual physical) possession suffices to maintain a partition action; a claimed tenant by the curtesy may properly be joined as a defendant and the burden of proving a child was born alive rests on the party claiming through that child.
notes: Real property partition/inheritance procedure dispute; no letting or lodging issue.

holding_summary: A restrictive covenant limiting a parcel to 'private dwelling house' use, made for the benefit of the original grantor's retained land, could not be enforced by a remote purchaser of a differently-restricted adjoining parcel because the covenant was never intended for that purchaser's benefit; the court therefore did not reach whether the proposed apartment house violated the covenant.
notes: Deed-covenant enforcement (privity/benefit) dispute over apartment-house construction; decided on covenant-benefit grounds without reaching any lodging/boarding characterization.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
holding_summary: Whether a landlord was negligent in maintaining a common water-closet used by upstairs tenement tenants, whose leakage damaged a ground-floor store tenant's goods, was a jury question; the no-duty-to-repair-demised-premises rule does not bar liability for negligence as to areas retained under the landlord's control.
notes: Landlord's-common-area negligence dispute in a mixed store/tenement building; not about the legal character or regulation of letting/lodging.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: Repairs made with the tenant's consent do not constitute an eviction or a surrender of the lease.
notes: One-paragraph landlord-tenant eviction/repairs ruling with no facts about lodging or boarding practice.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
holding_summary: A mortgagee who lawfully took possession of leased apartment property from an executor-landlord, and received an assignment of unpaid rent, stood in the conventional landlord relation to the tenant and could bring summary nonpayment proceedings; the tenant, having recognized the executor as landlord, could not challenge the sufficiency of the surrender to the mortgagee.
notes: Mortgagee-in-possession/summary-proceedings dispute over leased flat apartments; ordinary landlord-tenant rent collection, not lodging or boarding-house doctrine.
